transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well... I suppose I'm here because of the voices. I keep hearing them in my apartment. And... sometimes if I'm in an empty room at a museum, I hear them there, too. 

It's just... very clear voices. Like women, whispering from behind the walls. They keep telling me which photographs belong in the archive. That's... that's really all it is.
Do the voices tell you to do anything, or are they just commenting or providing information?
Like I said... they just tell me about the photographs. Which ones belong in the archive. They don't... they aren't making me do things. It's just that.
Do the voices feel like they are coming from inside your head or from outside?
Well... outside. Like I said, they're coming from behind the walls. In my apartment, or... those empty rooms at the museum. It's not in my head. I just hear them whispering out there.
Do you find yourself acting on the information the voices give you about the photographs?
No... I don't. I just... I hear what they say. I don't really do anything with it.
Do you experience any unusual smells, tastes, or feelings on your skin that aren't explained by anything around you?
No. I don't... I don't smell anything strange. Or taste anything. It's just the voices.
How long have you been hearing these voices?
It's been... about eight months now. That's when the voices started. And... when I knew for sure that people were watching my archive. About eight months.
Do you believe that people are actually watching your archive, or is that just a feeling you have?

I know they are. The museum board... the city arts people. They've been monitoring my phone. They know my Caribbean archive is going to change how the galleries tell the truth. It's not just a feeling. Nobody has shown me anything to prove they aren't.
Do you think the museum board or city arts people are watching you in person, or is it just your phone and archive they're monitoring?

I don't know about in person. I... I already told you, it's my phone. They don't need to follow me around when they can just monitor that. 

Because of the Caribbean archive. Like I said, they know it will change how the galleries tell the truth. And no one has shown me any proof that they aren't doing it. That's all I know.
Do you think the museum board or city arts people are trying to harm you or interfere with your life in any way beyond monitoring your phone and archive?

Harm me? I... no. I don't know about that. I haven't noticed them trying to hurt me. 

Just... just the phone. Like I said. I don't know what else they would be doing.
Do you find it hard to keep your thoughts organized when the voices are talking to you?

I don't... the voices? I guess. It's just hard to talk sometimes. Like when my cousin asks me about a bill, or a doctor's appointment. I try to answer, but I end up talking about the arts grant... and then the shipping routes... and my grandmother's altar. I just talk, and then I stop, and she just looks at me. She never knows what I mean. It just gets mixed up.
Do you find that your thoughts are difficult to follow or that you jump between unrelated topics when you're not hearing the voices?

I... I thought I just said that. It's like what I was just explaining about my cousin. 

It doesn't really matter if the voices are talking right then or not. She asks a simple question about a bill or an appointment, and... I just end up on the grant again. Or the shipping routes, or the altar. It just comes out. And by the time I stop, nobody knows what I meant. 

I don't really know what else to tell you about it.
Do you feel like your thoughts are disorganized most of the time, even when the voices are not present?

Yes. I... I feel like I just answered this. 

It's most of the time. Like I said, my cousin asks about an appointment, and I end up talking about the grant... or the altar. It happens even when it's quiet. 

I don't really know what else to say about it.
Do you ever have thoughts that don't make sense to you, or that seem to be unrelated to anything you're doing or talking about?

I really don't understand why you keep asking me the same thing. I... I just explained it to you. 

It's exactly what I just said. She asks about a bill, and I start talking about the grant... the shipping routes... my grandmother's altar. It's not related to the bill. I know that. But it's what comes out, and she doesn't know what I mean. 

I don't have anything else to tell you about it.
Do you believe the voices commenting on the photographs are specifically talking about you or your work?

I... I don't know if they're talking about me, exactly. 

It's just... I hear them. In my apartment. Sometimes when I go to the museum and the rooms are empty. It sounds like women, whispering. Coming from behind the walls. 

They just... they tell me which photographs belong in the archive. That's all. That's why I'm here.
Do you think your difficulty in keeping your thoughts organized is more troublesome to you than the voices you hear?

I don't... I don't really know how to compare them. 

They're just... they're both there. The whispering, the... the way my words get tangled up. I don't know which is worse. They just both happen.
Do you think your thoughts would be more organized if you weren't working on the Caribbean archive?

I don't think it has anything to do with the archive. It just happens. Like... like I said before. My cousin will ask me about a doctor's appointment, or paying a bill, and... I just start talking. About the grant money, or the boats, the shipping routes, my grandmother's altar. It just comes out that way. And then she just looks at me because she doesn't understand what I meant. It doesn't matter what I'm working on.
Do you believe there's anything unusual or special about you that sets you apart from other people?

I... I don't know about special. 

I just have days where I feel... radiant, I guess. Like I've been chosen. 

But then... if someone questions my plan, or tells me I need to slow down... I get furious. It just feels like they are trying to erase me. I don't really want to say more than that.
Can you tell me more about what you mean when you say you feel 'radiant' and 'chosen' on some days?

I... I don't know how else to explain it. It's just a feeling. I wake up and everything is just... bright. Like I have this big purpose. 

But... then people get in the way. If someone questions my plans, or... or tells me to slow down, I just become furious. It makes me so angry because... it feels like they're trying to erase me. That's... that's really all it is. I'd rather not keep talking about it.
Do you believe you have a special mission or purpose that sets you apart from others?

I... I thought I just said I didn't want to talk about this anymore. 

It's not a... a mission. It's just the work. My Caribbean archive is going to change how the galleries tell the truth. And they know it. The museum board, the city arts people... they know. 

That's why they've been monitoring my phone. I am convinced they are. People can say whatever they want, but no one has shown me a single thing that proves otherwise. I... I really don't want to say anything else about them.
Do you believe your Caribbean archive will have a significant impact on the world beyond just changing how galleries tell the truth?
I don't... I don't know about the rest of the world. I just know what it's supposed to do for the galleries. That's all I'm focused on.
